cards.explanation: The answer is the Spirit of the LORD. While the enemy sat in the valley, the Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon, Israel's leader (Judges 6:34). Right after that, Gideon blew the ram's horn and rallied the Abiezrites behind him. I think that's the best thing that can come upon a man when trouble moves in next door.

The answer is False. Gideon sent messengers throughout Manasseh, as well as Asher, Zebulun and Naphtali (Judges 6:35). Four places, not one. Gideon was NOT keeping that invite list small, friends, and the text says they came up to meet him.

The answer is dew only on the fleece and dry ground. Gideon said, “If there is dew only on the fleece and all the ground is dry, then I will know that You are going to save Israel by my hand, as You have said.” (Judges 6:37) That's a very particular order for one night, friends. Wet wool, dry floor.
The answer is a bowlful of water. Gideon squeezed the fleece and wrung out the dew, a bowlful of water (Judges 6:38). That's not a damp sock, friends, that's a real amount. The fleece was SOAKED.

The answer is True. After asking God not to be angry with him, Gideon asked for one more test (Judges 6:39). This time the fleece would be dry and the ground covered with dew. He turned it around from the first night.

The answer is False. The LORD told Gideon, “You have too many men for Me to deliver Midian into their hands…” (Judges 7:2). The army wasn't too small, friends, it was too big. Most generals never hear that one.

The answer is so Israel won't say their own hand saved them. The LORD said there were too many men “…lest Israel glorify themselves over Me, saying, ‘My own hand has saved me.’” (Judges 7:2) That's His stated reason, plain as that. The credit belongs where it belongs, friends.

The answer is most. Gideon announced that whoever was fearful and trembling could turn back, and twenty-two thousand did (Judges 7:3). Only ten thousand stayed. That's most of the army walking home, friends.

The answer is by how each man drinks the water. The LORD told Gideon, “Separate those who lap the water with their tongues like a dog from those who kneel to drink.” (Judges 7:5) The test was the way each man drank, friends. Nobody got a warning that this was a test, I bet.

The answer is three hundred. The number who lapped with their hands to their mouths was three hundred men, and all the others knelt to drink (Judges 7:6). Out of ten thousand, that's a tiny crew, friends. And the LORD planned to use them.

The answer is save. The LORD said, “With the three hundred men who lapped the water I will save you and deliver the Midianites into your hand.” (Judges 7:7) Three hundred men, and the LORD says He'll do the saving. That's a promise worth hearing, friends.

The answer is take his servant and listen in on the camp. The LORD said, “…go down to the camp with your servant Purah and listen to what they are saying.” (Judges 7:10 and 7:11) Then Gideon's hands would be strengthened to attack the camp. The LORD gave him a way to go down and hear for himself, friends.

The answer is a loaf of barley bread. The man said, “…I saw a loaf of barley bread come tumbling into the Midianite camp.” (Judges 7:13) Yes, friends, bread. Of all the things to see in a dream, a rolling loaf is quite the pick.

The answer is that God has given Midian to Gideon. The man's friend said, “God has delivered Midian and the whole camp into his hand.” (Judges 7:14) He called the loaf the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite. And Gideon was standing right there, listening, friends.
The answer is True. When Gideon heard the dream and its interpretation, he bowed in worship (Judges 7:15). Then he went back to the camp of Israel. He worshiped first and moved second, friends.

The answer is torch. Each man got a ram's horn in one hand and a large jar in the other, and inside the jar was a torch (Judges 7:16). A torch tucked inside a jar is a clever way to carry a light, friends. Horn in one hand, jar in the other, busy hands all around.

The answer is False. Gideon told his men, “Watch me and do as I do…” and, “…do exactly as I do.” (Judges 7:17) That doesn't sound like a man staying behind, friends. The text says Gideon and the hundred men with him reached the outskirts of the camp (Judges 7:19).

The answer is “For the LORD and for Gideon.” Gideon told them, “…shout, ‘For the LORD and for Gideon!’…” (Judges 7:18) When the moment came, they shouted, “A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!” (Judges 7:20). The LORD comes first in the cry, friends.

The answer is break them open. Gideon and the hundred men with him blew their horns and broke the jars that were in their hands (Judges 7:19). The other two companies shattered theirs too (Judges 7:20). The jars were hiding the torches, friends, so the breaking let the torchlight out.
The answer is False. Each Israelite took his position around the camp (Judges 7:21). They held the outskirts and made their noise from there, friends. And the entire Midianite army fled anyway.

The answer is True. The entire Midianite army fled, crying out as they ran (Judges 7:21). That's an army that had just heard three hundred horns, friends. I think nobody stopped to ask what was going on.

The answer is that the LORD turns the men against one another. When the three hundred rams' horns sounded, the LORD set all the men in the camp against one another with their swords (Judges 7:22). The three hundred didn't have to fight their way in, friends. The LORD did the work.

The answer is the Jordan. Gideon told the men of Ephraim to “…seize the waters of the Jordan ahead of them as far as Beth-barah.” (Judges 7:24) So all the men of Ephraim were called out, friends. And they captured the waters of the Jordan as far as Beth-barah.

The answer is on the other side of the Jordan. The men of Ephraim brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian, to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan (Judges 7:25). The text says they pursued the Midianites and then brought the heads to him, friends. So Gideon was across the river.
